unsupported_claims: Minor, non-operational and not load-bearing: the open-items list names 'the client platform (MT-X)' — no passage names MT-X; the bundle only names CLIMP and the mdm@lseg.com address. Also a generic gloss 'matching (the pairing of the two sides of a trade)' is added to Art. 58(1)(b), which only says 'the matching'. Neither is a field, time, version, fee, eligibility or legal-effect claim.
reason: Every substantive claim is entailed by the two evidence_only sections with correct locators (Articles 58–59, PDF 41–44 printed 40–43; Instructions §§1.1–1.2.3, PDF 7–10 printed 3–6) and review dates: the six Art. 59(1) categories, 'Issuers admitted pursuant to paragraph 1, letter e), take part in the Settlement Service solely for the purpose of settlement of free-of-payment transactions', the Consob/Bank of Italy agreement condition in Art. 59(3), and the indirect-participant test 'a) the customers fall under one of the categories referred to in paragraph 1, letters a), b) or c); b) ... securities accounts ... dedicated exclusively ...; c) the customer identification data ... known to Monte Titoli ...; d) limited to the entities referred to in paragraph 1 letter c) ...'. The '5 days' and '4 p.m.' figures, the LEI requirement and CLIMP routing are all in the Instructions excerpt, and the answer correctly surfaces the genuine discrepancy between Art. 59(6)(a) and the Instructions' footnote 1 ('Pursuant to article 6, of the Rules of the Settlement Service, may be qualify as Indirect Participants: a) Italian, EU and non-EU banks ... l) Italian Ministry of Finance') as a labelled inference plus unresolved requirement. Both LIMITATION lines ('Italian text prevails'; 'a firm's own eligibility requires its facts') are carried, and no specific client is certified — 'Whether your client qualifies is a matter of that client's own legal status and authorisations'.
